segments.english: 9) And you, our friend, it was not enough for you that you did not do any one of all these but you believed their words and accepted their lies on the testimony of one witness and one judge and not in the presence of the litigant without inquiry, without investigation, without examination and you enjoyed their words and you also helped to strengthen their lies and it was fixed in your mind as the truth itself until you wrote that I am no longer able to deny it, etc. And you did not take to heart that testimony is accepted only in the presence of the litigant and that you are obliged to inquire into them with seven inquiries, investigations and examinations, as you are commanded All the more so, since they did their deeds in the dark and smoothed their tongues to you in secret with their words to find a fault to hate and you were obliged to silence them with a rebuke. This is nothing but a wicked heart: that you enjoy and long for their gossip and their informing. the Merciful One save us from this opinion! And it is possible that you too add of your own false informing, in order to honor yourself at the disgrace of your friends. And in the chapter Arvei Pesachim (115) we read: "Rav Sheshet said in the name of R. A.: whoever tells evil talk and whoever bears false witness against his fellow deserves to be thrown to the dogs, as it is said: 'to the dog you shall throw it' and it is written explicitly: 'you shall not carry a false report'; and it is read in it: 'you shall not cause to bear'" And we find several more homilies of our Sages of blessed memory on the punishment of one who tells evil talk. "And in Mahzor Vitry, tractate Avot, on what we learned: 'do not judge your fellow until you reach his place' as he writes there: that the same transgression may come into your hand and you may be saved and escape from it as we find with Jeroboam son of Nebat that when Solomon married the daughter of Pharaoh, she brought in to him every kind of song in the world and said to him: 'So they do for such-and-such idolatry' One time, he went to sleep, and the day grew late she went and called the wood-carvers and the builders, who work at carving and weaving and they made over his bed the likeness of a firmament, and in it the sun, the moon, the stars and the constellations In the morning he woke from his sleep to open the doors of the Temple, for the keys of the Temple were under his pillow he saw that the firmament was bright with stars and the host thinking that the night had not yet turned he went back to sleep And he slept four more hours, until he understood and recognised for himself that the night was not so long And concerning that hour we learned a testimony about the morning daily offering, which is offered at four hours, in the Bechirta. Before he woke from his sleep, Jeroboam son of Nebat went to the door of his house and a voice went out: 'Wicked one how long will you sleep and neglect the morning daily offering What is it to you, sleeper? Arise, call upon your God!' A bat kol came out and said to him: 'Wicked son of a wicked man, you are destined to abolish from Israel many, many offerings wilfully. And you hold him liable for the inadvertent as for the wilful. And for the forced one as for the voluntary!' And this is what is written: 'When Ephraim spoke there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel, but he incurred guilt through Baal and died' This is said of Jeroboam, who was of the tribe of Ephraim, the trembling was the accuser against Solomon, he, Jeroboam, was prince in Israel and king and the bat kol answered him that he would become guilty through Baal and die." Thus far his words. And you have magnified and added to doing evil more than Jeroboam son of Nebat. For after you brought us to the prison by false informing before our exalted government! You called out all the people to go out to the cemetery, and commanded them to dust themselves with dust upon their heads for no reason. Not for a light commandment that we neglected, and not for a weighty commandment, God forbid, but because we walked in the custom of our forefathers and set our learning in the Mishnah and in the Talmud and the Rambam and Shulchan Aruch to learn and to teach, to keep and to do. And we did not study further from the forged book, the book the Zohar, as is your custom.

tokens.note: printed list marker "9)", kept as the author's own
ידידנו: "our friend", the ironic form of address, kept
לא דייך: "it was not enough for you"; the idiom governs the clause to 3:9.10
וכו': marks a truncated quotation; kept as "etc."
printed "והית" for "והיית" (and you were); the defective spelling is kept as printed
folio 115 of Pesachim, the reference as the author gives it (קי"ה)
ראב"ע: not expanded in the printed text; read as "R. A."; the full name is uncertain
תשיא: the reading the Talmud gives ("וקרי ביה"), set against the written לא תשא of Exod 23:1
לרז"ל: "our Sages of blessed memory"
על: the Mishnah's "al" (אל), the negative of "do not judge"
כ' ע"ש: "as he writes there"; the expansion is uncertain
לע"ז: abbreviation of עבודה זרה, "idolatry"
בבחירתא: transliterated; the source is not named in the pack
אלהיך: God of Israel, in the voice's words
מחייבו: the pointing does not fix the subject and object; both are kept as in the Hebrew
רתת: "trembled", the verse's word (Hos 13:1), read here by the author as the name of the accuser
קטיגורין: an accuser (the Talmudic term)
ח"ו: "God forbid"
ורמב"ם: the Rambam
וש"ע: the Shulchan Aruch
מזויף: "forged", the author's epithet for the Zohar
הזהר: "the book the Zohar", the title kept as the author writes it

grammar: לא דייך שלא עשית (3:9.5-7): an idiom, "it was not enough for you that you did not do". The irony turns on the reversal: the charge is not only the omission but the belief and acceptance that follow ("but", אלא).
בעד אחד ודיין אחד, ושלא בפני בעל דין, ובלא חקירה ובלא דרישה, ובלא בדיקה (3:9.16-29): the grounds of acceptance are listed in order, each negative with its own ובלא; the English keeps the repetition.

The Pesachim passage, after גרסינן, is Talmudic Hebrew with its own formulas (אמר רב ששת, כתיב בהדיא, וקרי ביה). It cites Exod 22:30 and Exod 23:1; the Talmud's reading (לא תשיא) is set against the written form (לא תשא).

The Mahzor Vitry passage runs from על הא דתנן to עכ"ל (thus far his words). The bat kol's speech sits inside it in single marks, and the verse of Hos 13:1 is its proof. The pronoun in ואתה מחייבו is left open, as the Hebrew leaves it.
The last part turns from the story to the addressee: ואתה הגדלת (and you have magnified) and כי אחרי אשר (for after) make the charge that his informing brought the author to prison.
segments.note: One paragraph (Wikisource, 1931 print). The printed list marker 9) is kept; the Hebrew abbreviations are expanded in the token glosses.
apparatus: Base text from Wikisource; the 1931 scan is not yet collated, so the reading is flagged here until it is (Q2 default).
Exod 22:30 (לכלב תשליכון אותו), quoted as written: "to the dog you shall throw it".
Exod 23:1 (לא תשא שמע שוא), quoted as written; the Talmud's reading לא תשיא is given as read (וקרי).
Hos 13:1 (כדבר אפרים רתת נשא הוא בישראל ויאשם בבעל וימות), quoted by the author; translated from the Hebrew.
The Mishnah quoted is named only as tractate Avot; the author writes על for אל. No chapter reference is added.
Pesachim: the author gives folio 115 only.
ראב"ע and כ' ע"ש are not expanded with certainty; the English gives the likeliest sense.
context: Bat kol: a heavenly voice, the rabbinic device by which a voice from heaven speaks to a person. Here it speaks to Jeroboam son of Nebat in the story the author cites from Mahzor Vitry.
